speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You are in my house at noon with a play still in front of you. Sit. I will not be told you are going to Carter Lane instead of your afternoon.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not going to Carter Lane instead of it. The carrier has been in since before noon. Hobbins can steam in the yard until I have done. Half past five is soon enough.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: A man at the pump said the Bell yard was full of horses before the clock had settled. Six, he thought, and all of them wet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Six is his number. They can eat their oats without me. I have an afternoon I am in, and I will not trade it for a letter that will wait an hour.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The letter is in your sleeve. I saw the corner of it. Three lines is a thin packet to keep a carrier standing, if you mean him to stand.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Three lines is what Sunday would bear. If there is a fourth, it will be written where he can see the ink, not here in a hurry. I am not inventing news I have not yet been given.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The loaf is a penny, and a full thumb short of the notch, if you are eating before you go back. The jaw took a crust yesterday. There is crust today, if you want it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will eat. I am mended enough for a house. What I do at another man's table tonight is that table's affair, not this loaf's.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Tonight is not my board, then. Threepence is today's dinner, all the same. The hall candle is not for a man who will be at Paul's after dark. Upstairs, when you come in, is yours.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will come in late. Do not sit up the firing for me. I know the sixpence, and I will not spend it on a supper I am not eating here.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Shall I put the three lines into a cover, so the horses do not see them?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave them as they are. A cover is a parcel, and a parcel is sixpence. A letter is twopence. I am sending a letter. I am not sending a bundle.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Twopence is an honest distinction. Mark me, Master Shakespeare. If Master Hobbins has a message from your wife that wants an answer, answer the message. Do not answer it with a play.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have never yet improved her letters by putting a play in them. I will not start at a table corner in the dark.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gib slept through your morning. He is awake now, and he is not invited to Carter Lane either.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He is wiser than a man who would skip a comedy for a horse. Let him be.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then eat, and go back, and do not come home by way of a story you could have posted. The latch is still the latch. Shut it when you are in, however late that is.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will shut it. I am not mending it. The afternoon is Navarre, and Navarre does not know about a carrier.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will keep a cup of something warm. Late is still a mouth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Keep it. If I have eaten elsewhere I will drink it, and if I have not, I will be glad of more than the drink.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Glad is not a plan. Half past five, you said. I will believe the hour when I hear the latch, and not before.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will tell the man at the pump, if he asks, that you knew about the horses and chose the play. He likes a story in which a lodger is late.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Tell him I am not late. Tell him the horses began without me, which is what horses are for.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: And tell him the afternoon is the master's own business. The pump has had enough of the horses.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Believe the play first. The Bell is the second errand. I have said so twice, and the horses will not shift me.
